notes: Overview: Large regional payments processor evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for production inference. Primary driver = regulatory control of PII and transaction data + predictable latency for fraud detection models.
Key quotes: "Cannot leave tokenized transaction logs in third-party storage — must be customer-controlled keys and clear retention policy." — Rahul (CTO)

Networking preferences: Strong preference for AWS PrivateLink endpoints into Redwood control plane; Transit Gateway acceptable if we can lock egress. No public internet-facing endpoints; all management traffic via customer-managed bastion/VPN.

Desired network controls (customer): port-level firewall rules (restrict to 443/8443 to Redwood endpoints), strict egress controls (block all outbound except to approved monitoring/SIEM IPs), IP allowlist for management CIDRs, NACLs + SG lockdown, NAT configuration for outbound-only flows.

PrivateLink vs Peering: Customer security prefers PrivateLink (endpoint services) for control plane metadata and to avoid cross-account routing. Peering considered for high-throughput data plane (model payloads) but needs additional routing controls and flow logs.

Egress considerations: Audit requirement to prevent exfil of raw PII. Proposal: egress gateway + proxy, explicit route tables for inference subnets, VPC flow logs to S3 + CloudWatch forwarded to Splunk (customer SIEM). Retention policy: 90 days for flow logs; application logs 30 days unless flagged for review.

KMS integration: Customer will provide a Customer-Managed Key (CMK) in their AWS account; require cross-account key policy and key grants for Redwood service principal. HSM-backed CMKs requested for transaction keys. Key rotation cadence and emergency rotation playbook requested.

Audit & compliance: Must emit audit logs for every model invocation (request id, sha of prompt template, model version, compute node id) to satisfy internal audit. Need proof of immutable audit stream and retention SLA for 1 year. SOC2 artifacts already reviewed but security team asked for runtime trace examples.

Security review checklist items outstanding: network diagram with subnet CIDRs, internal/external IP allowlist, private endpoint DNS resolution plan, KMS key policy draft, encryption-in-transit certs (mTLS) plan, pentest window scheduling.

POC success metrics: latency P95 < 250ms for inference path for 128-token prompts; throughput 100 reqs/sec with <10% tail latency increase; costs to be modeled by Redwood Optimize recommendations; no audit issues in first security sign-off.
Customer comments about rollbacks: want automatic model fallback to a quantized low-cost variant if primary fails; must be configurable and logged for audit trails.
Notes on procurement: Legal requires data residency clause (us-east-1 only) and ability to prove no logs persisted after retention window. Procurement timeline ~Q2 2026 if POC passes security review.

Short-term next steps (from call): team to submit completed security questionnaire by 2026-03-12; Redwood infra to produce final network diagram + endpoint IP ranges by 2026-03-15; schedule KMS policy workshop w/ security ops.
